FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A07
Obey the overhead indication for your lane; an arrow marked ONLY requires travel in that direction. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A07
Warning signs are generally yellow with black text or symbols, and most have a diamond shape. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A07
Warning signs call for slowing down and readiness to stop for a hazard or special condition. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A07
A five-sided black-on-yellow sign warns only of a school or school crossing; fluorescent yellow-green may also be used. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A07
At a school-warning sign, reduce speed, watch for children and stop when necessary. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A07
A round yellow sign with black markings warns in advance of a highway-rail crossing. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A07
At an advance rail-crossing warning, slow down and watch carefully, especially at night. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A07
A sharp-right-turn warning calls for reduced speed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A08
A winding-road warning calls for a speed adjustment. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A08
A yield-ahead warning calls for slowing and readiness either to stop at the yield sign or adjust to traffic. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A08
A bicycle warning on a shared road calls for looking in both directions for cyclists. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A08
A narrowing-road warning calls for slowing. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A08
A divided-highway-ahead warning directs drivers to keep right. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A08
At a warning of unpaved or unknown road surface, slow down and check vehicle control on the changed surface. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A08
Where the road has room for only one traffic lane, slow down and prepare to yield to opposing vehicles. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A08
A warning of a potentially hazardous two-lane passage calls for reduced speed and attention to opposing vehicles. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A08
An added-lane warning means merging is unnecessary, while attention to vehicles changing lanes remains necessary. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A08
For a steep hill, slow down and prepare to select a lower gear to manage speed and spare the brakes. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A08
The slippery-when-wet caption identifies the first half-hour of rain as the most hazardous period. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A08
A two-way-traffic warning marks the end of one-way operation and reminds drivers of opposing traffic. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A08
A bump warning calls for a speed adjustment to maintain control. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A09
A playground warning calls for caution because many children may be present. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A09
A deer-crossing warning calls for watching both sides of the road for deer. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A09
At a roundabout warning, reduce speed and yield to pedestrians and vehicles already circulating. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A09
A crossroad warning calls for attention to crossing vehicles and any regulatory signs or signals. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A09
An advisory-speed sign recommends a speed for its road section and is often mounted below another warning sign. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A09
A farm-machinery warning on a shared road calls for alertness and readiness to reduce speed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A09
A horse-drawn-vehicle warning calls for alertness and readiness to reduce speed. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A09
In a zipper merge, drivers use both lanes up to the lane-reduction point and then take alternating turns merging. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A10
Most guide signs are rectangular, with white lettering against green. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A10
A guide-sign arrow indicates the direction to the named destination. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A10
United States route markers use black numerals on a white U.S.-shield background. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A10
State route markers use black lettering on a white circle. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A10
An Interstate route shield has a red upper quarter with white Interstate lettering and a blue lower portion with a white route number. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A10
Motorist-service signs typically use white text against blue rectangles. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A10
Recreation signs generally have white lettering against brown. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A10
Flashing beacons can emphasize a sign or identify when its message applies. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A10
Beacons supplementing warning or speed-limit signs are yellow. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A10
Beacons supplementing Stop or Do Not Enter signs are red. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A10
Supplementary circular beacons flash regularly, at roughly one flash per second. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A10
A work zone is a highway area where construction, maintenance or utility activity takes place. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A10
Work-zone control devices begin ahead of the activity and extend past it. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R43 | anchor: A10
Work zones may stay in one place or move slowly along the road. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec08-R44 | anchor: A11
Work-zone traffic controls may include signs, arrow panels, pavement markings, cones, drums or barricades. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R45 | anchor: A11
Warning signs in work zones are usually orange. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R46 | anchor: A11
Stay alert in work zones for altered traffic patterns and slowing or stopped vehicles that may be hidden by a hill or curve. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R47 | anchor: A11
Drivers must follow work-zone police and flagger directions. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R48 | anchor: A11
A lane-closure warning calls for preparing to leave the closing lane. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R49 | anchor: A11
Work-zone speeding fines are doubled. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R50 | anchor: A11
In a work zone, avoid abrupt maneuvers and weaving, and brake gradually to give following drivers time to slow. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R51 | anchor: A11
Rough surfaces, metal plates, uneven lanes and pavement-edge drop-offs in work zones call for gradual, controlled movements. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R52 | anchor: A11
Maintain reasonable speed and following space in a work zone so slowing or stopped traffic leaves room to respond. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R53 | anchor: A11
Work-zone traffic may be stopped for alternating single-lane use, entering workers or machinery, or hazardous work. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R54 | anchor: A11
Temporary signals, police or certified flaggers with stop/slow paddles may control stopped work-zone traffic. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R55 | anchor: A11
Work-zone regulatory signs communicate speed limits and other rules, and limits may be reduced. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-R56 | anchor: A12
Work-zone warning signs are usually orange diamonds, with some rectangular signs also used. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-R57 | anchor: A12
Barricades, drums, cones and tubular markers warn of work-area hazards and guide traffic through the zone. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-R58 | anchor: A12
Channelizing devices often carry steady or flashing lights for nighttime visibility. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-R59 | anchor: A12
Flashing or sequencing arrow panels may guide traffic into selected lanes and warn of a road closure during day or night. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-R60 | anchor: A12
Work-zone flaggers stop, slow or guide traffic using red flags or stop/slow paddles. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-R61 | anchor: A12
The handbook describes work-zone flaggers wearing yellow-green shirts, jackets or vests. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0080]
